name: The Doors
hook: The Los Angeles band whose keyboard player covered the bass parts on stage, and who played on Weird Al's Doors pastiche forty years later.
blurb: The Doors formed in Los Angeles in 1965: Jim Morrison singing, Ray Manzarek on keyboards, Robby Krieger on guitar and John Densmore on drums. They signed to Elektra in 1966 and blended psychedelic rock, blues and acid rock. On stage they had no bass player: Manzarek played the bass lines on a keyboard. 'Light My Fire' (1967) went to number one, Elektra's first. After a concert in Miami on 1 March 1969, Morrison was arrested and convicted, and sentenced to six months with hard labour and a $500 fine; he was pardoned after his death, in 2010. He died in Paris on 3 July 1971, aged 27. The others made two more albums and ended the band in 1973. The RIAA counts 36 million albums sold in America.
